additions.description: GET /api/articles supports filtering by 'author' query parameter
additions.reasoning: The specification requires filtering articles by author username, which is implemented in the code. This is required, so not an addition.

additions.description: GET /api/articles supports filtering by 'tag' query parameter
additions.reasoning: The specification requires filtering articles by tag, which is implemented in the code. This is required, so not an addition.

additions.description: GET /api/articles and /api/articles/feed endpoints support 'limit' and 'offset' query parameters for pagination
additions.reasoning: The specification requires pagination support with limit and offset, which is implemented in the code. This is required, so not an addition.

additions.description: GET /api/articles and /api/articles/feed sort articles by article.id descending
additions.reasoning: The specification requires ordering articles by created timestamp descending, but the code orders by article.id descending, which is an implementation detail and not explicitly required.

additions.description: GET /api/articles/{slug} returns empty object {} when article not found
additions.reasoning: The specification states that GET after deletion returns 200 with empty object, which is implemented. This is required, so not an addition.

additions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug} deletes all comments of the article before deleting the article
additions.reasoning: The specification does not explicitly require deleting comments when deleting an article, but the code does so. This is an addition.

additions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug} clears article tags before deleting the article
additions.reasoning: The specification does not mention tag clearing on article deletion, but the code clears tags. This is an addition.

additions.description: GET /api/tags endpoint returns all tags as array of strings
additions.reasoning: The specification does not mention a /api/tags endpoint, but the code implements it. This is an addition.

additions.description: DELETE /api/users/{email} endpoint attempts to delete user by email and returns 500 on FK constraint error
additions.reasoning: The specification states that deleting a user with articles returns 500 due to FK constraint, but does not specify a DELETE /api/users/{email} endpoint. The code implements this endpoint, which is an addition.

additions.description: User dictionary includes 'id' field in response
additions.reasoning: The specification does not require returning user 'id' in responses, but the code includes it in user_dict. This is an addition.

omissions.description: POST /api/users does not validate email format or password strength
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires user creation with valid email and password, but the code only checks presence, not format or strength.

omissions.description: POST /api/articles does not validate required fields title, description, body presence
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires these fields for article creation, but the code uses default empty strings without validation.

omissions.description: PUT /api/articles/{slug} does not allow updating slug or enforce slug immutability
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires slug to remain unchanged on update, but the code does not update slug and does not explicitly enforce immutability.

omissions.description: PUT /api/articles/{slug} does not allow non-owner users to update articles (returns 403), but specification shows any user can update/delete any article
omissions.reasoning: The specification demonstrates a security vulnerability allowing any user to update/delete any article, but the code enforces ownership checks and forbids non-owners.

omissions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug} does not allow non-owner users to delete articles (returns 403), but specification shows any user can delete any article
omissions.reasoning: Same as above for delete operation.

omissions.description: GET /api/articles and /api/articles/feed do not order articles by created timestamp descending as required
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires ordering by created timestamp descending, but the code orders by article.id descending.

omissions.description: GET /api/articles/feed returns articlesCount 0 and empty array if user follows no one, as required
omissions.reasoning: This is implemented as required, so no omission.

omissions.description: POST /api/articles/{slug}/comments does not validate comment body presence or non-empty
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires comment body, but the code accepts empty string without validation.

omissions.description: DELETE /api/articles/{slug}/comments/{id} allows deletion only by comment author or article author, but specification does not specify this restriction
omissions.reasoning: The specification does not mention comment deletion authorization rules, but the code restricts deletion to comment author or article author.

omissions.description: POST /api/profiles/{username}/follow does not prevent user from following themselves (no 400 error)
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires 400 error when user tries to follow themselves, but the code allows it silently.

omissions.description: DELETE /api/profiles/{username}/follow does not prevent user from unfollowing themselves (no 400 error)
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires 400 error when user tries to unfollow themselves, but the code allows it silently.

omissions.description: GET /api/articles does not return 'created' and 'updated' timestamps in response article object
omissions.reasoning: The specification requires 'created' and 'updated' timestamps in article responses, but the code returns 'createdAt' and 'updatedAt' only.

omissions.description: PUT /api/user does not validate uniqueness of updated username or email against other users
omissions.reasoning: The code checks for existing username/email but does not handle race conditions or partial updates robustly.
